page: Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8280M processor running at 2.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 instructions. The server is equipped with 1024 GB of system memory, providing a high density of 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Additionally, it includes 2097 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, including single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, falls into the bottom 10 percent. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as demonstrated by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory subsystem performance is a highlight, with large-block uncached read bandwidth reaching a strong 215.58 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent. Other memory operations, database transactions, and Redis SET operations perform at average levels.

Given the massive 1 TB memory allocation and substantial local storage, the M64s offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The trade-off is lower single-core compute efficiency, making it less suitable for single-threaded tasks or latency-sensitive sequential processing. It is best suited for large-scale databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: The Microsoft Azure M64s is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8280M processor, 1024 GB of RAM, and 2097 GB of local storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 16 GB of memory per vCPU and a 105 MB L3 cache. Benchmarks reveal a trade-off: single-core CPU performance is limited, ranking in the bottom 10 percent, whereas multi-core execution and database operations reach average tiers. Notably, uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is strong at 215.58 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25 percent. Lacking a GPU, this server is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads rather than parallel acceleration. It is highly suited for large-scale databases, in-memory data stores, and heavy data processing pipelines that require massive memory capacity over high single-threaded clock speeds.
